claims.statement: Allocation rule v18 creates split-reservation exceptions (EXC-0921) that perfectly correlate with held orders on east node: 100% of held orders are in EXC-0921; no non-EXC-0921 orders are held
claims.corroboration: Exception audit identifies EXC-0921 scope with perfect correlation; e03 confirms v18 implements split-reservation behavior to east node
claims.limitation: Cannot yet distinguish whether split-reservations themselves cause the hold, or whether v18's routing to east node exposes a capacity/carrier constraint

next_action.rationale: Examine what changed in v18 regarding split-reservations. Determine if split-reservations are: (1) expected behavior but with a downstream defect in carrier integration, (2) an unintended side-effect of the east-first reservation logic, or (3) benign but only on non-east-node lanes. This will confirm whether the split-reservation itself is the root cause or whether it's a valid allocation pattern that exposed a separate constraint.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Establishes whether v18's split-reservation behavior is anomalous (supporting allocation_rule_defect as root cause) or expected (pointing to downstream carrier/dock constraint as actual cause)
